record.paper_title: Open problems in the theory of completely positive and copositive matrices
record.original_question: Given a completely positive matrix A, determine or estimate its cp-rank cpr(A), defined as the minimum number of columns in an entrywise nonnegative matrix B such that A = B B^T.

evidence.quote: Finding the cp-rank of a given completely positive matrix, or estimating it, is a basic open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A real symmetric matrix $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ is called completely positive if there exists an entrywise nonnegative matrix $B \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times k}$ (for some $k \ge 1$) such that $A = BB^{T}$. The cp-rank of such a matrix, denoted $\operatorname{cpr}(A)$, is defined as the smallest integer $k$ for which such a nonnegative factorization $A = BB^{T}$ with $B \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times k}_{\ge 0}$ exists.

Problem: Given an arbitrary completely positive matrix $A$, develop a method to determine the exact value of $\operatorname{cpr}(A)$, or otherwise to provide tight upper and lower estimates for $\operatorname{cpr}(A)$ in terms of computable invariants of $A$ (such as its order $n$, its rank, its sparsity pattern, or other structural data).
artifact.status_search_result: Determining the cp-rank of a given completely positive matrix remains a basic open problem. Deciding complete positivity is known to be NP-hard (Dickinson–Gijben), and while the maximal cp-rank over n×n completely positive matrices is now known to be ⌊n²/4⌋ for n ≥ 5 (Bomze–Schachinger–Ullrich, with refinements through 2023–2024), efficient algorithms for computing the cp-rank of an individual matrix are not available. Recent work (e.g., 2024 results on the 5×5 cone and polynomial-time algorithms for fixed-r checks) provides partial progress but no general solution.

status_evidence.title: The Cone of 5×5 Completely Positive Matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical algorithm to compute the cp-factorization for 5×5 matrices, illustrating the difficulty of the cp-factorization problem.
status_evidence.claim: Computing cp-factorizations (and hence cp-rank) is computationally difficult even for small orders.

status_evidence.title: A polynomial-time algorithm for computing low CP-rank decompositions
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomial-time algorithm for checking if a PSD matrix has cp-rank at most r for fixed constant r.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial (fixed-r) polynomial-time algorithms exist; the general cp-rank computation problem is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: On the cp-Rank and Minimal cp Factorizations of a Completely Positive Matrix
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of cp-rank and minimal cp factorizations.
status_evidence.claim: The exact computation of cp-rank for general completely positive matrices remains a research problem.
